datasets.title: Deconvolution of regulatory T cell heterogeneity identifies cycling precursors as conductors of immune escape during breast carcinoma progression
datasets.summary: Tumor-immune microenvironment is instrumental in shaping breast cancer tumor evolution. We previously identified an evolutionary bottleneck demarcating ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) from invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). How the microenvironment evolves during such transition remains elusive. We dissected, in parallel, single-cell composition of DCIS and IDC patients and rat tumors that faithfully recapitulate human breast cancer. We discovered T cell diversity distinguishing DCIS and IDC and a novel cycling Treg state occupying the pseudotime bifurcation between DCIS and IDC, preceding more activated Treg subtypes. Multiscale analysis of patient cohorts as part of HTAN Consortium established that cycling Treg predicts recurrence in low-grade DCIS. We proved cycling Treg as Treg progenitors critical for immune escape and demonstrated that OX40 agonism restored immunotherapeutic sensitivity, where responders displayed increased inflammatory CAF subtype heterogeneity. Our study thus established cycling Treg’s importance in preserving immune escape and underscored its prognostic value to stratify future recurrence.
datasets.overall_design: Dataset 1: Breast tissues of patients (DCIS, IDC) or healthy individuals (Normal) were subjected to tissue dissociation via collagenase 4/hyaluronidase and FACS sorted for immune, epithelial, myoepithelium, and stroma compartment based on lineage markers and later to droplet-based 10X scRNAseq (3'HTv3)/Illumina NovaSeq6000. Dataset 2: Outbred Sprague Dawley rats were injected with NMU carcinogen (50 mg/kg, twice, 7 days apart, starting at 40 days of age rat) to induce rat mammary tumors. Tissues from mammary glands (MG) of untreated rats or NMU-treated rats and progressing tumors from NMU-treated rats were dissociated by collagenase 4/hyaluronidase, FACS-sorted for immune, epithelium, and stroma fractions, and subjected to droplet based 10X scRNAseq (3'HTv3) pipeline and Illumina NovaSeq6000. Dataset 3: Rats treated with NMU as aboved were subjected to three immunotherapy regimens (+isotype control) right when NMU-tumors became palpable. The rats were treated by anti-OX40 agonist (every 48hr, 2.5 mg/kg, till sacrifice) or anti-PDL1 (every 7 days, 10.0 mg/kg, till sacrifice) or combination of anti-OX40 and anti-PDL1 or isotype (same dosage). Responding versus Non-Responding tumors of each treatment were dissociated by collagenase 4/hyaluronidased and selected for scRNAseq 10X pipeline (5'HTv2)/Illumina NovaSeq6000. Raw reads from dataset 1 were aligned with the human genome hg18 while reads from dataset2/3 were aligned with the Sprague Dawley rat reference genome (Rnor_6). Downstream analyses of Datasets 1-3 include basic filtering and quality control, removal of cell doublets, batch-effect control/integration, cell cluster identification, Milo neighborhood analysis, Trajectory inference by Monocle3, Coexpression hub analysis, GSEA, CellChat, etc.

datasets.title: Short and long-term effects of CDK4/6 inhibition on early stage breast cancer
datasets.summary: CDK4/6 inhibitors are used in the treatment of advanced estrogen receptor (ER)(+) breast cancer (BC). Their efficacy in ER(-) and early stage BC is currently under investigation. Here, we show that palbociclib, a CDK4/6 inhibitor, can inhibit both progression of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and growth of invasive disease in both an ER(-) basal BC model (MCFDCIS) and an ER(+) luminal model (MCF7 intraductal injection). In MCFDCIS cells palbociclib repressed cell cycle gene expression, inhibited proliferation, induced senescence and normalized tumorspheres formed in Matrigel whilst the formation of acini by normal mammary epithelial cells (MCF10A) was not affected. Palbociclib treatment of mice with MCFDCIS tumors inhibited their malignant progression and reduced proliferation of invasive lesions. Transcriptomic analysis of the tumor and stromal cell compartments showed that cell cycle and senescence genes, and MUC16, an ovarian cancer biomarker gene, were repressed during treatment. Knockdown of MUC16 in MCFDCIS cells inhibited proliferation of invasive lesions but not progression of DCIS. After cessation of palbociclib treatment genes associated with differentiation, e.g. p63, inflammation, IFNγ response and antigen processing and presentation remained suppressed in the tumor and surrounding stroma. We conclude that palbociclib can prevent progression of DCIS and is anti-proliferative in ER(-) invasive disease mediated in part via MUC16. Lasting effects of CDK4/6 inhibition after drug withdrawal on differentiation and the immune response could impact the approach to treatment of early stage ER(-) breast cancer.
